title: helmstudio registry entry
description: One file per studio in the registry, as studios/<id>.yaml. An entry is a pointer: it says where a studio's repository is and which ref to read, and the manifest itself lives in that repository as helmstudio.yaml. The inline `manifest` exists only for a repository that does not ship one yet; when it starts to, the pull request that moves `ref` removes the inline copy, so there is still exactly one copy of the truth. There is deliberately no `certified` field: a certification level is derived from what has actually been checked, never declared by the thing being checked (docs/design/05-sdk-and-custom-studios.md §9, docs/decisions.md M7 Q4 and Q15).

schema_version.description: Registry entry schema major. Omitted means 1.

id.description: The studio's id, the same slug its manifest carries. The file is named for it.

repo.description: git clone URL. helmstudio reads it with git and never through a forge's HTTP API, so any transport git understands works. The approval preview names the transport before anything is cloned.

ref.description: Branch, tag or commit to read. It is resolved to a commit before anything is shown or built, and what gets installed is that commit — so a branch that moves after a preview was approved does not change what runs.

manifest.description: The studio's manifest, inline, for a repository that ships no helmstudio.yaml of its own. Where it sets `id`, `repo` or `ref`, each must equal the pointer's — a rule the validator enforces, because JSON Schema cannot compare two fields. A repository that ships its own manifest wins over this one, and this one is then dead weight to be deleted.
